evidence_for_selection_review.finding: A Tianjin inquiry links changing Chinese terminology, imperialism and urban life; one case does not cover China or Asia.
Indigenous health historiography explicitly addresses race/colonialism, correcting a practitioners-only picture. Body unavailable; a bounded abstract-level claim stays visible.

evidence_for_selection_review.locator: medical05_recovered, Wynter et al. version-of-record pp. 2–3
evidence_for_selection_review.finding: The authors themselves identify sidelined clinicians and cite broader-voice programmes by Ana Antić and Martin Summers; this identifies follow-up literature without making clinicians article authors.

evidence_for_selection_review.locator: medical_geo05_sources1, Machado/Gomes Portuguese Resumo and Gomes da Silveira abstract
evidence_for_selection_review.finding: Brazilian urban/territorial work and critique of northern disciplinary histories provide contrasting regional evidence. Portuguese abstract is read in the original; the 2024 survey is English-language.
Black women’s spatial knowledge and contestation are substantive claims, not a token roster mention. Distinct from colonial administrators’ policy categories in Harris.
Explicitly plural and multilingual programme identifies Chinese and Italian reviews and warns against linguistic nationalism. The programme’s existence does not establish successful inclusion.

investigated_omissions.subject: Latin American/Caribbean medical history: Cueto and Palmer
investigated_omissions.evidence: batch-05 publisher introduction summary; new raw/access-checks.json
investigated_omissions.outcome: Deferred proposal retained. English sample again timed out; indexed Spanish translation metadata surfaced but body URL returned 404. No claim of body recovery or new 2025 original work.
investigated_omissions.next_action: Recover authorized introduction or author abstract; preserve Adriana Soldi translation credit when that version is used.

investigated_omissions.subject: Enslaved Black and Irish immigrant women in Cooper Owens’s medical history
investigated_omissions.evidence: batch-05 JSTOR publisher description and recorded failed body requests
investigated_omissions.outcome: Deferred due to argument-evidence scope; these patient histories remain an important gap, not interchangeable with a study of psychiatric professionals.
investigated_omissions.next_action: Recover a selected authorized passage or author abstract; retain coercion and patient-agency qualifications.

investigated_omissions.subject: Chinese and Italian historical-geography scholarship
investigated_omissions.evidence: Legg et al. p. 6 and note 7
investigated_omissions.outcome: Named leads: Yannan Ding’s 2021 review; Nicola Gabellieri’s Italian review; Ruohong Li, Xiaohong Zhang and Shuang Li’s Chinese review. The editorial is read, the reviews themselves are not.
investigated_omissions.next_action: Read the named surveys and relevant original-language sources before deriving their arguments.

investigated_omissions.subject: Broader histories of colonial and transcultural psychiatry
investigated_omissions.evidence: Wynter et al. p. 3 cites Ana Antić (2022) and Martin Summers (2010)
investigated_omissions.outcome: Specific literature leads retained, no new claims attributed to unread works.
investigated_omissions.next_action: Reconcile work identities and retrieve the cited programmes.

unresolved_gaps: Medical coverage remains uneven across Latin America, South Asia, Africa and the Pacific; retaining earlier Vaughan/Feierman/Janzen contexts does not establish their post-2000 coverage.
Patient, nursing, midwifery, hospital and pharmaceutical histories are not covered by the selected psychiatry/colonialism cases.
English-accessible sources remain dominant; one Portuguese abstract and English accounts of China/Brazil do not establish original-language breadth.
Harris’s imperial-policy analysis is not Indigenous territorial authority or direct testimony.
No exhaustive discovered-person denominator or sourced demographic classification exists. Do not report a gender balance percentage or use author-name inference.
Nine works do not complete either field through 2026. All eighteen selected authors participate in work-specific claims through explicit authorship; no full-node promotion is required.
